baseline_abstract: Understanding and modelling vaccination effectiveness is important for national health policy. Health-economic analyses that lump chronological age and dose history can conceal age- and dose-dependent risks, particularly in young children. We formulate a hybrid age--calendar transport framework combining state-transition dynamics, continuing births, scheduled-dose interfaces and population feedback. We combine deterministic ordinary differential equation (ODE) and stochastic continuous-time Markov representations: matched ODEs efficiently compute expected counts, while the stochastic interpretation characterises conditional variability and event probabilities. We state the conditions linking these representations, derive characteristic and population balances, and show why dose-state aggregation generally fails to close. A five-state pneumococcal conjugate vaccine application provides a monthly implementation and numerical refinement study. Controlled Markov experiments verify expected occupancies and quantify terminal-count variation and absorption probabilities; a separate closed-cohort simulation checks matched discrete-time expected rewards. Populations with identical age and dose marginals produced different indirect multipliers and disease-event totals. Manufactured-solution and submonthly experiments quantified numerical behaviour. For three separately evaluated products, delayed/incomplete dosing, attained-age waning and gradual indirect-protection build-up jointly reduced quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gains by 10.2--18.4\%; paired herd-off comparisons attributed 61.0--69.7\% of full-scenario gains to the modelled indirect pathway. Schedule experiments and deterministic perturbations demonstrate how the retained structure changes programme comparisons. The framework offers readers a reproducible connection between model representations and a way to identify information needed for programme evaluation. The economic results remain conditional illustrations: empirical calibration, verified valuation inputs and joint parameter uncertainty are required before policy prediction.
